source: KS-32 OS v3.01, routines 0xC1C7E8 (ESP init at boot) and 0xC1C8C0/0xC1C8E4 (effect program load); hand-transcribed from the disassembly
addressing: ESP host register n is at CPU address 0x260001 + 2*n (odd bytes). DUART at 0x280001 + 2*n; DUART reg 0x0E = set-output-port-bits, 0x0F = reset-output-port-bits; OP6 is ESPHALT.
host_write_protocol: Before writing a select register ($80/$A0/$C0/$E0) while running, poll host reg $16 (PC) until PC < 0x28 (skipped while halted, flag $DE7F)
Write the select register, then poll host reg $12 bit 2 (Host Access OK/) until 0; timeout ~2x31 polls -> error 0x21 (33, 'bad ESP chip' in the service manual)
GPR writes of SPRs/params are verified by read-back via $80 and retried up to 10 times (routine 0xC1CC80)
When finished, read-select is parked at 0xC0 (non-GPR) as the datasheet recommends (0xC1CC74)

boot_init.meaning: GPR+INSTR write to 0x9F with whatever the latches hold
host control: RAM clear + refresh disable
host serial control: SLAVE, SONY, SER3=out, SER2/1/0=in

program_load.meaning: fade output level GPR 0x7F (used by every program) to 0
type 1/2/3/4 records of the program (esp/esp_programs.json); includes MEMSIZ/DLENGTH/SIGREG/ABASE/BBASE writes
only for a program that writes ABASE/BBASE (index 10): RAM access ctl $14=0x7F (write RAM), DOL=$0C/$0D word, DADR $0F/$10 = word address, $11 = 0; then read back with $14=0xFF and compare
read every record back; mismatch -> reload, up to 10 times, then error
levels from table 0xC0A72C indexed by sound/effect parameters, ramped
